source_caption:
Thomas Haden Church spent months working out for Spider-Man 3 to physically transform into Flint Marko, but many of Sandman’s most emotional moments come from the opposite of spectacle: his quiet guilt and sadness. Sam Raimi treated him less like a simple villain and more like a tragic figure, which is why his origin scene remains one of the film’s most memorable sequences.

Spider-Man 3 (2007), directed by Sam Raimi, starring Tobey Maguire, Kirsten Dunst, James Franco. A darker and more chaotic superhero sequel that pushes Peter Parker through revenge, guilt, and inner corruption as new enemies force him to confront the worst parts of himself.

source_details.title: Spider-Man 3
source_details.synopsis: Spider-Man 3 is a 2007 American superhero film directed by Sam Raimi, who co-wrote it with his brother Ivan and Alvin Sargent. Based on the Marvel Comics character Spider-Man, it is the final film in Raimi's Spider-Man trilogy and the sequel to Spider-Man 2 (2004). Tobey Maguire stars as Peter Parker / Spider-Man, alongside Kirsten Dunst, James Franco, Thomas Haden Church, Topher Grace, Bryce Dallas Howard, James Cromwell, Rosemary Harris, and J. K. Simmons. Set a year after the events of Spider-Man 2, the film follows Peter as he prepares for his future with his girlfriend Mary Jane Watson, while facing the Sandman, Venom, and his vengeful friend Harry Osborn.
